verdict.rationale: First-party docs cover the core of the story. Tool use (function calling) works with user-defined tools, and strict tool use guarantees schema validation of tool names and inputs. Claude calls multiple tools in parallel by default, all current models support tool use, and the Messages API is positioned for custom agent loops, with tool results returned to the model (e.g., the bash tool) and fine-grained tool-input streaming. missing for 10: explicit documentation of the multi-step tool-result loop beyond the bash-tool example, independent or hands-on corroboration that tool calling is faithful in practice.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can rely on faithful function/tool calling — typed tool definitions, parallel and multi-step calls — documented well enough to run an agent loop on this model

citations.quote: Tool use (also called function calling) lets Claude call functions that you define or that Anthropic provides
Strict tool use (`strict: true`): Guarantee schema validation on tool names and inputs
By default, Claude may call multiple tools in a single response
Best for: Custom agent loops and fine-grained control
Let Claude request shell commands that your application runs in a persistent bash session and returns as tool results.
All current models support text and image input, text output, multilingual capabilities, vision, and tool use.
